messages:
david.customer: Hi, our production app started returning HTTP 400 from your /v1/call-function endpoint this morning when functions return structured args in JSON mode. Error: "Invalid function arguments: argument 'items' expected array of objects with 'id' keys". This started after a weekly model flip.

alice.support: Sorry about that — can you paste the request body you sent and the exact error response body? Also which model and model version are you using?

david.customer: Here's the request we sent (redacted key):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call-function \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{
    "model": "open-xlarge-2025-06",
    "function": "order_batch_processor",
    "json_mode": "strict",
    "args": {
      "order_id": "ord_9933",
      "items": "[{\"id\": \"sku_123\", \"qty\": 2}]"
    }
  }'

And the service responded 400 with body:

{
  "error": "Invalid function arguments: items must be an array of objects"
}

This worked fine yesterday. :confused:

alice.support: Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) can you confirm whether the model is returning a JSON string for `items` (i.e. double-encoded) or returning an actual array? 2) can you share the function declaration schema you registered with the function?

ben.oncall: Looping in ops-bot logs — giving us the request/response pair and the inference payload. ops-bot: payload-id=pid_7788 model=open-xlarge-2025-06 route=hosted-us-east latency_ms=215.

ops-bot: inference-output-snippet: "...calling function order_batch_processor with args: {\"order_id\": \"ord_9933\", \"items\": \"[{\\\"id\\\": \\\"sku_123\\\", \\\"qty\\\": 2}]\"}..."

alice.support: That looks like the model produced a JSON-encoded string for `items` (double-encoded). Two paths: we can coerce/deserialize at the runtime boundary, or we can tighten the schema enforcement to reject string->array coercions. Which would you prefer?

charlie.eng: Quick root-cause analysis — the function schema declared `items` as `array<object { id: string, qty: integer }>` and our JSON-mode parser is currently strict for arrays. The model's assistant response included `items` serialized as a string (model produced `"[{...}]"`). We have a migration in runtime that toggled `auto_deserialize_json_strings` to false last week to avoid silent coercions for other customers. That likely explains the sudden break after model flip.

alice.support: For immediate mitigation, I can flip `auto_deserialize_json_strings` to true for your org so the runtime will attempt to parse stringified JSON in args before validation. Would that be acceptable? It may mask other latent schema issues but will restore compatibility.

charlie.eng: Longer term, recommend two fixes: 1) show clearer error with path to offending field, e.g. `items: expected array, got string`; 2) add a policy option per route: `coerce_stringified_json: true|false` (default false). I'll open a patch.

david.customer: Flipping the runtime option sounds fine for now. We need a hotfix — customers in EU are hit. Also would be great if you can provide a repro script so we can test compatibility with future model flips.

alice.support: Done — I enabled `auto_deserialize_json_strings` for your org (org_id=org_447). Try the same request again and confirm. Also attaching a minimal repro below.

--- repro.sh ---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
API_KEY=REDACTED
cat <<'REQ' | curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call-function \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d @-
REQ

{
  "model": "open-xlarge-2025-06",
  "function": "order_batch_processor",
  "json_mode": "strict",
  "args": {
    "order_id": "ord_9933",
    "items": "[{\"id\": \"sku_123\", \"qty\": 2}]"
  }
}

--- end repro ---

ben.oncall: David — after the flip I see a 200 now with runtime deserializing. Response: "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"processed\":1}". Can you confirm full e2e? :thumbsup:

david.customer: Confirmed, batch processed. Thanks! Can you also add a note in the console about `coerce_stringified_json`? We want to avoid relying on it permanently.

charlie.eng: I'll file ENG-7642 to add console UI and a route-level toggle and also a monitoring alert that flags repeated string-to-array coercions (indicates model drift). Adding a short patch to improve error text in the next minor release.

alice.support: Closing this thread as resolved for now. If it recurs please DM me and we'll escalate SLA if needed. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: ticket=SUP-9981 org=org_447 severity=high assigned=alice.support
